title: Initiative horizon map and OKR deconfliction guide
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As we scale Redwood's product lines (Hosted, Dedicated, Private), company-level OKRs are generating overlapping initiatives that compete for the same engineering and design capacity. Without a lightweight, repeatable process to phase initiatives and resolve conflicts, teams spend cycles negotiating priorities during crunch planning weeks.

Goal: Create an "initiative horizon map" and a short playbook for OKR deconfliction that product, design, and engineering leads can use during quarterly planning and cycle syncs. Deliverables: 1) a template horizon map (3 horizons: Now/Next/Later) with lane definitions and gating criteria, 2) a decision rubric that ranks initiative priority using outcome impact, customer risk, compliance/regulatory urgency, and operational cost, 3) a handoff/cutover checklist for multi-quarter initiatives, 4) a proposed Linear/Console setup (labels, parent links, dashboard widgets) to operationalize the flow.

Scope: Company-level OKRs and initiatives that touch two or more teams. This playbook intentionally excludes single-team tactical work and long-term research projects (R&D runway > 12 months).
acceptance_criteria: A reusable horizon map template saved in Confluence with examples for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private use-cases
A 5-point decision rubric (scored) and tie-breaker rules documented and agreed by PM/Eng/Design leads
Three scenario playbooks: (a) competing initiatives with limited Eng capacity, (b) regulatory urgent initiative requiring preemption, (c) incremental rollouts across Dedicated and Private
Linear configuration notes (labels, parent_issue conventions, dashboard queries) published and applied to next planning cycle
Executive sign-off from VP Product and VP Engineering on gating criteria and escalation path
notes: Early trade-off: strict prioritization reduces context-switching but may under-serve niche enterprise customers; rubric weights need calibration with Customer Success input.
Decision to keep the horizon model shallow (3 lanes) vs. complex multi-tier horizon: chose 3 lanes for clarity in cross-org meetings.
We will prioritize tooling changes that are low-effort (Linear labels, Console dashboard) before investing in a custom orchestration service.
Security/compliance edge case: Private/on-prem initiatives that require audit or KMS changes should get an automatic priority bump in the rubric (see regulator_urgency factor).
